question.:question/problem:

$\frac{2}{x^{6}}+\frac{4}{\sqrt[5]{x^{6}}}-5x^{2}.$ For real $x\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int\left(\frac{2}{x^{6}}+\frac{4}{\sqrt[5]{x^{6}}}-5x^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &= \int\left(2x^{-6}+4x^{\frac{-6}{5}}-5x^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &= 2\int x^{-6}\,\mathrm{d}x+4\int x^{\frac{-6}{5}}\,\mathrm{d}x-5\int x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &= 2\left(\frac{x^{-6+1}}{(-6+1)}\right)+4\left(\frac{x^{\frac{-6}{5}+1}}{(\frac{-6}{5}+1)}\right)\\ &\quad -5\left(\frac{x^{2+1}}{(2+1)}\right)+C\\ &= -\frac{2}{5x^{5}}-\frac{20}{\sqrt[5]{x}}-\frac{5x^{3}}{3}+C.\end{aligned}
